title: Leeds beat West Ham in shoot-out to reach FA Cup semis for first time in 39 years
byline: Leeds reached the FA Cup semi-finals for the first time in 39 years as they survived a dramatic penalty shoot-out after squandering a two-goal lead in a thrilling clash with West Ham on Sunday.

title: Rice and curry, kottu, fried rice prices up
byline: Following the recent rise in domestic LP gas prices, the All Ceylon Restaurant Owners’ Association has announced that the prices of several popular food items, including rice and curry packets, fried rice and kottu, will be increased by Rs. 20.

title: Chinese national arrested over Kohuwala murder
byline: A 26-year-old Chinese national has been arrested by the Western Province South Crime Division in connection with the murder of a Chinese woman in Kohuwala on March 23, 2026.

title: 12-hour water cut imposed in Homagama and surrounding areas
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board said that water supply to Palanwaththa and the surrounding areas in Homagama will be interrupted from 8.00 p.m. today (06) until 8.00 a.m. tomorrow (07), due to prevailing dry weather conditions.

title: Rishini Weeraratne bags Platinum Excellence Award
byline: Rishini Weeraratne, Editor of ’The Sun’, was honoured with the Platinum Excellence Award for Media Influence, Storytelling, and Women’s Empowerment at the Platinum Excellence Awards 2026, held at Cinnamon Life, Colombo.

title: NDB Bank fraud shock deepens to Rs. 13.2 bn
byline: National Development Bank PLC (NDB) said an internal fraud has been quantified at about 13.2 billion Sri Lankan rupees, sharply higher than earlier estimates.

title: No Cabinet discussion on extending judges’ retirement age: Justice Minister
byline: Expressing his views on opposition politicians’ allegations that the Government is planning to extend the retirement age of Supreme Court and Court of Appeal judges, Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara told the Daily Mirror that the Cabinet of Ministers has not discussed anything in that regard.

title: Three villagers trampled to death in Anuradhapura
byline: Increasing the death toll in the human-elephant conflict in the Anuradhapura district, three villagers- two of them in Eppawala and the other in Priyankaragama- had been trampled to death by wild elephants last mroning. They had died at the scene.

title: Fuel stocks sufficient for festive season; No price revisions planned: CPC
byline: The Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) has assured the public that fuel shipments are arriving as scheduled, ensuring stable supplies through the upcoming festive season. Managing Director of the CPC Mayura Neththikumara said that there are currently no plans to revise fuel prices during this period.

title: Oil prices choppy after expletive-laden Trump threat to Iran
byline: Oil prices saw choppy trading on Monday morning in Asia after US President Donald Trump threatened to destroy critical infrastructure in Iran unless it allows ships to cross the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Police to strictly enforce traffic laws during festive season
byline: Police said that traffic laws will be strictly enforced across the country during the festive season.

title: Cardinal makes swipe at Donald Trump on Easter Sunday, questions his Christianity
byline: In an obvious swipe at US President Donland Trump over the US-Israeli war on Iran, Archbishop of Colombo Cardinal Malcolm Ranjith said all nations are suffering today because of selfishness of one man who wants to rule the world.

title: Trump issues expletive-laden threat to Iran over Hormuz Strait blockage
byline: US President Donald Trump has published an expletive-laden post on social media in which he threatened to destroy Iran’s power plants and bridges if it failed to meet his Tuesday deadline to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to all shipping.

title: The 40 minutes when the Artemis crew loses contact with the Earth
byline: No-one will have been further from home than the Artemis astronauts.

title: Vidya’s murderer attempts sexual assault again
byline: One of the seven persons who gang-raped and murdered schoolgirl Sivaloganathan Vidya in Jaffna is 2013 is alleged to have attempted to sexually abuse a lady doctor on duty at the prison in Pallekelle, Kandy where he is kept since conviction.

title: KKR under pressure ahead of Punjab test in IPL 2026
byline: The 2026 Indian Premier League has begun with a tightly packed table, as several teams sit level on points after the opening round, with net run rate already shaping the early standings.

title: Iran demands war compensation to reopen Strait of Hormuz: Official
byline: Seyyed Mehdi Tabatabaei, deputy for communications at the Iranian president’s office, has said Iran will open the Strait of Hormuz only after receiving compensation for war damages, paid via a “new legal regime” based on transit fees.

title: Trump threatens ’’crazy b***s’’ of Iran and demands reopening ’’f***g strait’’ of Hormuz before Tuesday
byline: The president of the United States, Donald Trump, launched this Sunday his toughest warning to date, loaded with insults, against the authorities of Iran after the blockade of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. He has given them until next Tuesday to reopen the passage or, otherwise, assures that he will order a massive attack against the country’s main infrastructures.

title: WHO chief raises concerns over US-Israeli attacks on nuclear sites in Iran
byline: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, director-general of the World Health Organisation, has raised the alarm over the safety of nuclear facilities in Iran following US-Israeli strikes close to the Bushehr nuclear power plant.

title: 15 ships Transit Strait of Hormuz in 24 hours
byline: A total of 15 ships passed through the Strait of Hormuz over the past 24 hours after obtaining permission from Iran, according to a report by Iran’s semi-official Fars News Agency.

title: Iran, US receive plan to end hostilities, immediate ceasefire, source says
byline: Iran and the United States ​have received a plan to end hostilities that could come into effect on Monday and ‌reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a source aware of the proposals said on Monday.

title: National QR Payment Promotion Programme launched
byline: Sri Lanka took a major step towards a digital economy with the launch of the “National QR Payment Promotion Programme” today (06) under the patronage of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake.

title: Patients in the lurch as doctors, health ministry lock horns
byline: Patients across the country are bearing the brunt of an escalating standoff between the Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA) and health authorities as a bitter dispute over post-internship appointments spirals into a full-blown crisis.

title: Subashini, Sri Lanka-born Tamil actress, dies
byline: Shocking news has emerged from the Tamil TV industry. Popular actress Subashini Balasubramaniyam breathed her last today, on April 6, 2026. Following a family conflict, the actress reportedly took her own life by hanging herself. She took this step just a few days before her birthday. Subashini committed suicide at her residence in Chennai.

title: Kenya records 7.9 million tourists in 2025 as sector earns Ksh.500 billion
byline: The government has revealed that Kenya welcomed an estimated 7.9 million tourists in 2025, comprising 2.7 million international visitors and 5.2 million domestic travelers.

title: Trump says open the’’f***g Strait’’, Iran mocks ’we’ve lost the keys’
byline: Tehran has taken a sharp swipe at US President Donald Trump after his repeated threats to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with the Iranian Embassy in Zimbabwe sarcastically claiming it had “lost the keys.” Reacting in similar vein, Iran’s embassy in South Africa joked: “Shh… the key’s under the flowerpot.  Just open for friends.

title: Iran reviewing peace proposal but not open to ‘temporary ceasefire,’ senior official says
byline: Iran won’t reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for a “temporary ceasefire,” a senior Iranian official tells Reuters, adding that Tehran views Washington as lacking the readiness for a permanent ceasefire.

title: Police issue urgent cybersecurity warning for festive period
byline: The Police have issued an urgent warning to the public regarding a surge in sophisticated online financial fraud and data theft during the Sinhala and Hindu New Year festive period. As more citizens turn to the internet for holiday shopping and payments, cybercriminals are increasingly using deceptive tactics to steal money and sensitive personal information.

title: Strike kills IRGC intelligence chief, Iranian state media reports
byline: The chief of intelligence in Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has been killed in a strike, the IRGC announces.

title: Lightning strike damages house in Point Pedro
byline: A house in the Point Pedro Grama Niladhari Division in the Jaffna District was partially damaged following a lightning strike this evening.

title: CSE ends volatile session in green as geopolitical sentiment improves
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange opened the week with a volatile trading session on 06th March 2026, initially trending lower amid escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, which weighed heavily on investor sentiment. In response, market participants adopted a cautious “wait-and-see” approach, resulting in subdued activity during the first half of the session.

title: Government to provide Rs. 100 subsidy on diesel: President
byline: The government has decided to provide a subsidy of up to Rs. 100 on diesel after considering market price fluctuations, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said today.

title: Water supply restrictions announced in Homagama amid dry weather conditions
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) has introduced restrictions following the prevailing dry weather, as reservoir levels continue to decline.

title: India’s Vice President to visit Sri Lanka
byline: The Vice President of India C. P. Radhakrishnan is scheduled to undertake a two-day official visit to Sri Lanka, President’s Media Division (PMD) said.

title: Over 10,000 child protection complaints reported in 2025
byline: A total of 10,455 child protection complaints have been reported in 2025, reflecting a growing number of concerns raised by the public, according to the National Child Protection Authority (NCPA).

title: Suresh Salley files writ petition challenging arrest and detention
byline: Former Director of the State Intelligence Service, Major General Suresh Salley, has filed a writ petition before the Court of Appeal challenging the legality of his arrest and detention in connection with investigations into the Easter Sunday attacks.

title: CAA ramps up raids ahead of festive season amid price hike fears
byline: Authorities have intensified islandwide raids targeting price exploitation and hoarding, as concerns grow over potential shortages and price hikes ahead of the upcoming festive season.

title: Govt cancels weekly Wednesday holiday
byline: The government has announced the cancellation of the weekly Wednesday holiday granted to public sector offices, with effect from April 8.

title: LAUGFS secures LPG shipment to ensure uninterrupted festive supply
byline: LAUGFS Gas PLC has received a 7,000 metric ton LPG shipment via the vessel ANDOVER at its terminal in Hambantota Port, boosting nationwide supply ahead of the upcoming festive season.

title: Iran says US airman rescue may have been cover to ‘steal enriched uranium’
byline: Iran’s foreign ministry says the US operation to rescue a downed airman may have been a cover to “steal enriched uranium” from the country.

title: Yala leopard “Lucas” killed? probe launched
byline: A major controversy has erupted over the fate of Yala’s famed male leopard “Lucas,” with authorities launching an investigation into claims that the big cat may have been run over or possibly targeted in a suspected safari jeep incident inside Yala National Park.

title: Artemis II astronauts have toilet trouble on their way towards the Moon
byline: Nasa is set to send humans deeper into space than ever before, but there’s one piece of technology that still has some kinks - the Orion space capsule’s toilet.

title: Emergency jabs after 100 children die of suspected measles in a month in Bangladesh
byline: Bangladesh has launched an emergency vaccination campaign after a fast-spreading measles outbreak is suspected of killing more than 100 people, mostly children, in what may be the country’s most lethal wave of the disease in recent history.

title: Israel strikes Iran’s petrochemical complex at Asaluyeh, defence minister says
byline: Israel struck Iran’s largest ​petrochemical complex at Asaluyeh on ‌Monday, defence minister Israel Katz said, in what he described ​as a severe economic ​blow to Tehran.

title: 2024 census final report presented to President
byline: The final report of the Census of Population and Housing 2024 was officially presented today (06) at the Presidential Secretariat to Anura Kumara Dissanayake by Census and Statistics Department Director General K. M. D. S. D. Karunarathne.

title: Iran says US airman rescue may have been cover to ‘steal enriched uranium’
byline: Iran’s foreign ministry says the US operation to rescue a downed airman may have been a cover to “steal enriched uranium” from the country.
